workflow_title: Screening mammography interpretation with BI-RADS assessment and MQSA-mandated reporting and patient communication
occupation_scope: Mammography interpreting physician (breast imaging radiologist); radiology technologist acquires the images
workflow_summary: The interpreting physician reads screening mammograms, assigns the ACR BI-RADS final assessment category and breast tissue density, and issues a report that meets MQSA-mandated contents plus patient lay-summary letters and timely communication of suspicious results.
source_reference: PRIMARY: 21 CFR 900.12 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/900.12, full text fetched) mandates the interpreting workflow: physician qualification and experience requirements (240 examinations in 6 months initial, 960 in 24 months continuing), standardized report contents with final assessment categories (Negative, Benign, Probably Benign, Suspicious, Highly Suggestive of Malignancy, Known Biopsy-Proven Malignancy, Post-Procedure Marker) plus incomplete categories, breast density in 4 categories, patient lay-summary letters (30 days, 7 days if Suspicious or malignant), and provider communication within 30 days. SUPPORTING: ACR BI-RADS page (https://www.acr.org/Clinical-Resources/Clinical-Tools-and-Reference/Reporting-and-Data-Systems/BI-RADS, fetched) documents the ACR BI-RADS reporting system and lexicon.
expert_raw_materials: Digital mammography DICOM images (CC and MLO views), prior studies for comparison, patient clinical history, ACR BI-RADS Atlas assessment criteria, facility audit data
usage_permissions: Images accessible within the MQSA-certified facility medical record (21 CFR 900.12); ACR BI-RADS Atlas materials used under ACR licensing for institutional reporting (ACR BI-RADS page)
task_input: Screening mammogram image set with indication and any prior images
professional_operations: Verify image quality and compare with priors; interpret findings on a certified workstation; assign the BI-RADS final assessment category (0-6) and tissue density category; dictate the structured report; issue the lay-summary letter within MQSA deadlines; arrange recall or biopsy communication when suspicious (7-day letter); record audit outcomes for the facility audit
expected_deliverable: Signed structured imaging report with BI-RADS category and density, a patient lay-summary letter, and provider notification when indicated
success_criteria: Correct BI-RADS categorization audited against biopsy outcomes, compliance with MQSA notification deadlines (7 and 30 day rules), interpretable lay letter, facility audit targets met under MQSA oversight
verification_approach: MQSA facility audits and medical outcome audits; double reading where adopted by the program; correlation of BI-RADS 4 and 5 with pathology; peer review of discordant cases
platform_dependencies: Certified mammography acquisition unit; DICOM PACS plus a reading workstation, which is institutional Windows infrastructure per typical practice; dictation and BI-RADS lexicon tooling; a MQSA-compliant patient letter system
blocking_risks: Reading requires FDA-certified display systems and institutional PHI access; the lay-letter and 7-day communication rules are mandatory MQSA compliance obligations; interpretation depends on certified radiologist judgment, and the PACS workstation is an interactive non-Linux institutional GUI, so the workflow needs a task redesign before any Linux-based automation
expert_capability: Mammography qualification under MQSA (240 initial and 960 continuing examinations), BI-RADS lexicon mastery, breast density assessment skill
cross_domain_overlap: clinical_informatics builds the reporting and letter systems rather than the interpretation. No S1-02A overlap, the A round contains zero health candidate rows.
granularity_check: Right granularity: a bounded day-scale interpretation and reporting task, not a career and not a single micro-action.
pending_confirmation: No critical gaps. Optional: confirm current ACR BI-RADS Atlas 5th edition category wording with ACR clinical resources staff.
data_usage_authorization: Mammography devices and image data are regulated under MQSA (21 CFR 900.12, https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/900.12); image data belongs to the medical record and is used under facility policy and patient authorization; ACR BI-RADS material is used under ACR terms (https://www.acr.org/Clinical-Resources/Clinical-Tools-and-Reference/Reporting-and-Data-Systems/BI-RADS)
privacy_considerations: Mammography reports and lay letters contain PHI; US processing is governed by HIPAA with de-identification per 45 CFR 164.514 expert determination or identifier removal (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514); MQSA itself mandates patient-direct communication, so handling of identifiable patient letters is intrinsic to the workflow
research_ethics: Retrospective use of mammography images for model research requires IRB approval under 45 CFR 46.111 criteria including risk minimization and consent waiver provisions (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.111); false-negative misses and overdiagnosis are the documented dual-use and incidental finding concerns of this workflow
reproducibility_assessment: BI-RADS assessment categories are a standardized lexicon, so the report skeleton is reproducible; inter-reader variability is the main non-black-box risk and facility audits measure it; automation must reproduce the published lexicon criteria instead of a proprietary model (https://www.acr.org/Clinical-Resources/Clinical-Tools-and-Reference/Reporting-and-Data-Systems/BI-RADS)
primary_claim: 21 CFR 900.12 sets the complete interpreting workflow: physician experience requirements, standardized report contents and final assessment categories, breast density reporting, and patient lay-summary plus provider communication deadlines.

workflow_title: Lung-RADS v2022 category assignment and follow-up management recommendation for lung screening LDCT
occupation_scope: Thoracic (chest) radiologist in a lung cancer screening program; the pulmonologist or primary clinician receives the report
workflow_summary: A radiologist reads a screening low-dose chest CT, compares it with prior studies, assigns the Lung-RADS assessment category plus the S modifier from nodule size and features, and issues the recommended follow-up management interval.
source_reference: PRIMARY: ACR Lung-RADS v2022 manual PDF (https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/americancoldf5f-acrorgf92a-productioncb02-3650/media/ACR/Files/RADS/Lung-RADS/Lung-RADS-2022.pdf, downloaded and read) defines the categories and management: category 0 Incomplete with prior CT comparison needed and 1-3 month LDCT; category 1 Negative with 12-month LDCT; category 2 benign features; category 3 Probably Benign; category 4A Suspicious for a solid nodule of at least 8 to less than 15 mm; plus the S modifier for added suspicion features (spiculation, lymphadenopathy, GGN size doubling). SUPPORTING: ACR Lung-RADS page (https://www.acr.org/Clinical-Resources/Clinical-Tools-and-Reference/Reporting-and-Data-Systems/Lung-Rads, fetched).
expert_raw_materials: Low-dose CT DICOM series, prior screening CTs for comparison, Lung-RADS category and management tables, nodule measurement tools
usage_permissions: Screening images under the institutional medical record; Lung-RADS use follows ACR terms in US screening program settings (ACR Lung-RADS page)
task_input: A low-dose CT lung screening study with prior examinations referenced for comparison
professional_operations: Assess technical adequacy; compare with the prior CT and assign category 0 when comparison is unavailable; measure the nodule and characterize features (solid or ground glass, spiculation, lymphadenopathy); assign the Lung-RADS 0 to 4X category plus S modifier; determine the management interval (12-month LDCT, shorter interval LDCT, or diagnostic workup); sign the structured screening report
expected_deliverable: A Lung-RADS structured report with category, modifier, and follow-up management recommendation
success_criteria: Correct category assignment against nodule outcomes, screening program cancer detection targets, and timely recommended follow-up intervals
verification_approach: Program-level lung screening audits; second review of suspicious cases; registry outcome correlation such as the ACR Lung Cancer Screening Registry
platform_dependencies: Low-dose capable CT scanner; PACS with prior-comparison and measurement functions; screening tracking or registry submission (ACR LCSR); structured reporting template
blocking_risks: Category assignment needs comparison priors and standardized measurement inside the institutional PACS; any nodule CAD the program deploys must be FDA-cleared, which is a conditional path; Lung-RADS version updates force template changes
expert_capability: Thoracic imaging interpretation, nodule measurement and characterization per Lung-RADS, prior-comparison discipline
cross_domain_overlap: clinical_informatics builds the registry and reporting tooling; the oncology tumor board (med_onco_wf04) consumes the findings. No S1-02A overlap, the A round has zero health rows.
granularity_check: Right granularity: a bounded per-study categorization task recurring at day scale.
pending_confirmation: Confirm the categories beyond the downloaded 2-page summary document (the category table is verified; remaining lexicon detail should be cross-checked with the full ACR manual via ACR).
data_usage_authorization: Screening CT data are used under institutional protocol and patient authorization; Lung-RADS manual usage follows ACR terms (https://www.acr.org/Clinical-Resources/Clinical-Tools-and-Reference/Reporting-and-Data-Systems/Lung-Rads); in the US, lung screening is CMS-covered with registry reporting obligations
privacy_considerations: CT screening reports contain PHI; US processing is governed by HIPAA with de-identification per 45 CFR 164.514 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514); registry submission is de-identified per program rules
research_ethics: Research on screening image cohorts requires IRB approval under 45 CFR 46.111 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.111); incidental findings outside the lung are a documented ethics point in screening and must be reported per program policy
reproducibility_assessment: Lung-RADS is a standardized lexicon with explicit size thresholds, so category assignment is rule-reproducible apart from reader variability in measurement and feature calls; the S modifier encodes the suspicion factors; automation must reproduce the published thresholds and categories (https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/americancoldf5f-acrorgf92a-productioncb02-3650/media/ACR/Files/RADS/Lung-RADS/Lung-RADS-2022.pdf)
primary_claim: The ACR Lung-RADS v2022 manual defines the screening LDCT interpretation workflow: assessment categories 0 through 4X with associated findings and the management recommendation for each category (for example 12-month LDCT for category 1, 1-3 month LDCT for incomplete comparison).

workflow_title: Synoptic histopathological reporting of breast cancer resection specimens to the RCPath G148 dataset
occupation_scope: Consultant histopathologist (breast pathologist); biomedical scientists perform specimen dissection and block selection
workflow_summary: A histopathologist examines a breast resection specimen grossly and microscopically, records the core data items required by the RCPath G148 dataset (tumour size, grade, margins, receptor and HER2 status, lymph node status), and issues a synoptic proforma report with TNM8 staging that drives treatment decisions.
source_reference: PRIMARY: RCPath G148, Dataset for histopathological reporting of breast disease in surgical excision specimens of breast cancer, November 2024, PDF served at https://www.rcpath.org/resourceLibrary/g148-dataset-for-histopathological-reporting-of-breast-disease-in-surgical-excision-specimens-of-breast-cancer.html (downloaded, 239 pages, read in part): defines core data items, a synoptic proforma template, TNM8 staging appendices and SNOMED coding, and states that the recorded invasive carcinoma features drive treatment decisions. SUPPORTING: CAP Cancer Protocols page (https://www.cap.org/protocols-and-guidelines/cancer-protocols/current-cancer-protocols/, fetched) documents the US-equivalent synoptic protocol program.
expert_raw_materials: Resection specimen slides and blocks, gross examination notes, specimen request form, RCPath dataset proforma, TNM8 tables, SNOMED CT codes
usage_permissions: RCPath datasets are published standards distributed free on rcp.org.uk for pathology service use under College terms; specimen examination occurs under the patient treatment consent
task_input: A breast surgical resection specimen (lumpectomy or mastectomy) with clinical context and prior biopsy results
professional_operations: Perform gross examination and block taking per protocol; measure and grade the tumour; assess margins, vascular invasion, oestrogen and progesterone receptor and HER2 status; sample lymph nodes; complete the synoptic proforma with the graded core data items; assign TNM8 stage; issue the structured report into the hospital system
expected_deliverable: A synoptic breast pathology report conforming to the G148 core data items with TNM8 stage and SNOMED coding, delivered to the multidisciplinary team
success_criteria: Report contains all mandatory core data items (G148 completeness standard); tumour grade, margins and node status correct as verified by audit and peer review; report available where the multidisciplinary team can act on it
verification_approach: RCPath external quality assessment and laboratory audits of dataset completeness; double reporting of cancer cases; multidisciplinary team review against imaging and surgery
platform_dependencies: Histology laboratory (fixation, embedding, staining, immunohistochemistry for receptors and HER2), a laboratory information system with synoptic reporting templates, dictation; NHS laboratories additionally use specified SNOMED codes
blocking_risks: Receptor and HER2 testing depend on laboratory instrumentation; synoptic templates live in proprietary LIMS products, so automation is conditional on the LIMS vendor; dataset updates (G148 November 2024) require template re-approval
expert_capability: Breast histopathology subspecialty training, G148 dataset compliance, TNM8 staging and SNOMED coding
cross_domain_overlap: med_onco_wf04 tumor board consumes this report as input; clinical_informatics supplies the LIMS. No S1-02A overlap, the A round has zero health rows.
granularity_check: Right granularity: a bounded per-case reporting workflow recurring daily, not a career.
pending_confirmation: Confirm current G148 usage and licensing terms with the RCPath publications office; optional, confirm with CAP that US protocols remain the CAP-facing analogue.
data_usage_authorization: Pathology data are collected under treatment consent and processed under laboratory accreditation (UKAS ISO 15189 in the UK); the RCPath dataset governs the required data items and its use is under RCPath terms (https://www.rcpath.org/resourceLibrary/g148-dataset-for-histopathological-reporting-of-breast-disease-in-surgical-excision-specimens-of-breast-cancer.html)
privacy_considerations: Pathology reports contain identifiable patient data. US processing is governed by HIPAA with de-identification per 45 CFR 164.514 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514); UK processing of NHS pathology data falls under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, while EU member states apply the GDPR special categories for data concerning health (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32016R0679), so no single global rule applies
research_ethics: Retrospective use of pathology slides and tissue requires IRB or research ethics committee approval with minimal risk review under 45 CFR 46.111 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.111) in the US and NHS research ethics approval in the UK; consent for secondary research use follows local policy and archival tissue raises consent-scope questions
reproducibility_assessment: G148 fixes mandated data items and a proforma, so the report structure is highly reproducible; interobserver variability concentrates in grade and margin calls, which the dataset criteria exist to reduce; digital slides make AI-assisted scoring reproducible where the dataset criteria are machine-checkable (https://www.rcpath.org/resourceLibrary/g148-dataset-for-histopathological-reporting-of-breast-disease-in-surgical-excision-specimens-of-breast-cancer.html)
primary_claim: The RCPath G148 dataset (November 2024) documents the whole breast resection reporting workflow: specimen examination, the core data items to record (tumour characteristics, receptors, margins, nodes), the synoptic proforma format, TNM8 staging, and SNOMED coding.

workflow_title: CLIA proficiency testing enrollment, blind sample testing, and performance evaluation for nonwaived laboratory tests
occupation_scope: Laboratory director is the responsible party; medical laboratory scientists run the samples; the proficiency testing coordinator manages enrollments
workflow_summary: A nonwaived clinical laboratory enrolls each regulated analyte in a CMS-approved proficiency testing program, runs PT samples through the routine patient-testing process, submits results, and reviews the program grading to detect and correct test performance problems.
source_reference: PRIMARY: 42 CFR 493.801 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/493.801, full text fetched): the laboratory must enroll in an HHS-approved PT program for each specialty and subspecialty, test PT samples in the same manner as patient specimens, designate the programs, notify CMS of any change, and authorize the PT program to release compliance data to HHS. SUPPORTING: 42 CFR 493.941 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/493.941, full text fetched): hematology PT grading criteria, for example cell identification must match the consensus of 80 percent of at least 10 referee laboratories or 80 percent of participants, WBC differential within 3 standard deviations of the target, erythrocyte count within 4 percent, hematocrit within 4 percent.
expert_raw_materials: Proficiency testing challenge samples from the approved provider, sample handling logs, instrument output records, PT event summaries and evaluation reports
usage_permissions: PT program enrollment contracts with CMS-approved providers; the CLIA certificate for nonwaived testing; the authorization to release compliance data to HHS required by 42 CFR 493.801
task_input: Shipped PT samples for each regulated analyte plus the event schedule
professional_operations: Enroll and maintain enrollment for each specialty and subspecialty; receive and check the samples; integrate PT samples into routine runs in the same manner as patient specimens; report results to the PT program by the deadline; receive grading; investigate and remediate any failure; retain records for inspection
expected_deliverable: Completed PT event submissions plus a compliant participation record with documented corrective actions
success_criteria: Passing PT scores per analyte per event, for hematology per 42 CFR 493.941 (80 percent consensus, 3 SD differential, 4 percent erythrocyte and hematocrit limits); no unsolved failure; continuously compliant enrollment
verification_approach: PT program grading; CMS inspection of records; laboratory director review of every event summary; documented corrective actions after failures
platform_dependencies: Analyzer instrumentation; the laboratory information system for result capture; PT program web portals; a document retention system
blocking_risks: PT providers are commercial external web portals; LIS-to-portal interfaces vary by vendor; analytical instruments are proprietary and need vendor middleware, so automation is conditional on those interfaces
expert_capability: Laboratory director oversight under CLIA personnel qualifications; technologist competency in the regulated analytes
cross_domain_overlap: clinical_informatics supplies the LIS; public_health uses proficiency data for surveillance. No S1-02A overlap, the A round has zero health rows.
granularity_check: Right granularity: a recurring per-analyte regulatory workflow at quarterly or biannual cadence.
pending_confirmation: No critical gaps. Optional: confirm the current CMS-approved PT provider list with the CMS CLIA program.
data_usage_authorization: PT compliance data are governed by CLIA, including the 42 CFR 493.801 authorization to release compliance data to HHS (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/493.801); PT samples are anonymized test materials owned by the PT provider
privacy_considerations: PT samples carry no patient PHI, but instrument runs and logs co-mingle patient data that are subject to HIPAA in the US with de-identification per 45 CFR 164.514 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514)
research_ethics: Reuse of PT event data for research such as proficiency benchmarking requires IRB review where individuals could be traced, under 45 CFR 46.111 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.111); PT sample use in methods research is covered by provider terms
reproducibility_assessment: PT grading criteria are quantitative and published in 42 CFR 493 subpart I (80 percent consensus, 3 SD and 4 percent limits, https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/493.941), so evaluation is fully reproducible; the lab-side flow (same-manner testing and deadlines) is procedural and checkable
primary_claim: 42 CFR 493.801 defines the complete PT participation workflow: enrollment in HHS-approved programs per specialty, testing samples in the same manner as patient specimens, program designation and change notification, and authorization to release compliance data to HHS.

workflow_title: Incidental pulmonary nodule risk categorization and follow-up scheduling using the Fleischner Society 2017 guidelines
occupation_scope: General or thoracic radiologist reading routine CT; findings communicated to the ordering clinician
workflow_summary: A radiologist detects an incidentally found pulmonary nodule on CT, measures its size and morphology, refines patient risk, and per the Fleischner Society 2017 recommendations assigns a follow-up CT interval or a no-follow-up decision, documented in the report.
source_reference: PRIMARY (fetched and read): Scholtz et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2017, PMC5903561 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5903561/) reproduces the 2017 incidental pulmonary nodule management recommendations including the size-risk follow-up table logic (solid nodules of 4 mm or less, 5, 6-8, and above 8 mm split by low and high risk; subsolid nodules below 5 mm and 6 mm or more; multiple subsolid nodules; high-risk features such as smoking, age above 60, upper-lobe location, spiculation, nodule size above 20 mm). CANONICAL: MacMahon et al., Fleischner Society 2017, Radiology 2017;284(1):228-243 (publisher full text not fetchable from this environment this round).
expert_raw_materials: CT DICOM series, nodule measurements, smoking and age risk inputs, Fleischner follow-up interval tables
usage_permissions: CT data handled under institutional medical record policy; the guideline text is cited from the open-access PMC copy of the application review
task_input: A routine chest CT containing an incidentally detected pulmonary nodule
professional_operations: Detect and measure the nodule; classify solid, part-solid or ground-glass morphology; refine patient risk from history (smoking, age, location, spiculation, size); select the recommended follow-up interval or no-follow-up from the Fleischner tables; document findings and recommendation in the report; communicate to the ordering clinician
expected_deliverable: A CT report with the incidental nodule description, risk classification, and the recommended follow-up interval
success_criteria: Recommended interval matches the guideline tables for the measured size and risk class; malignant nodules are not discharged to no-follow-up; benign nodules avoid unnecessary imaging
verification_approach: Second reader review of incidental findings; retrospective audit of follow-up timeliness; pathology correlation for progressed nodules
platform_dependencies: PACS with measurement tools; institutional reporting template embedding the guideline tables; follow-up tracking in the EHR or radiology worklist
blocking_risks: Measurement tools live inside the proprietary PACS; nodule diameter versus volume measurement variability must be handled; the canonical Radiology 2017 full text sits behind a publisher wall, so the tables should be re-verified before regulatory use
expert_capability: Cross-sectional chest imaging interpretation, nodule measurement, guideline table application
cross_domain_overlap: Lung-RADS screening interpretation (med_diag_wf02) is close but distinct: screening LDCT category assignment versus incidental nodules on routine CT; they share nodule measurement but different populations and tables. No S1-02A overlap.
granularity_check: Right granularity: a bounded per-examination measurement and scheduling task.
pending_confirmation: Confirm the reproduced follow-up tables against the canonical Fleischner Society guidelines in MacMahon et al., Radiology 2017;284(1):228-243, via institutional access; escalate to the coordinator or a thoracic radiologist.
data_usage_authorization: CT data are used under institutional medical record policies; the guideline content is cited from the open-access application review at PMC5903561 which licenses redistribution for reuse (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5903561/)
privacy_considerations: Nodule findings are PHI within CT records; US processing under HIPAA with de-identification per 45 CFR 164.514 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514); in the EU and UK, patient imaging falls under GDPR or UK GDPR data-concerning-health provisions (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32016R0679), so the applicable rule depends on jurisdiction
research_ethics: Retrospective nodule-cohort research requires IRB approval and consent-waiver review per 45 CFR 46.111 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.111); incidental findings must be disclosed per institutional policy; overdiagnosis from aggressive follow-up is an ethics-relevant consequence
reproducibility_assessment: The Fleischner size and risk tables are deterministic, so the decision step is reproducible from the published thresholds; the main variability source is nodule measurement (diameter versus volume) and risk refinement; automation must reproduce the exact published table values (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5903561/)
primary_claim: The Fleischner Society 2017 recommendations, as reproduced and applied in the fetched open-access article, define the incidental pulmonary nodule workflow: measure nodule size and features, refine patient risk, and select the recommended CT follow-up interval or exit from follow-up using published size-risk tables.

workflow_title: Radiation therapy physics plan and chart review: initial plan and chart check, weekly check, and end-of-treatment check
occupation_scope: Qualified medical physicist performs the checks; the dosimetrist supports computation; the radiation oncologist approves the plan
workflow_summary: A medical physicist performs structured verification of a radiation treatment plan and chart: checks the prescription and dose limits, reviews target and organ-at-risk contours and dose distributions, verifies quality assurance measurements, and then performs weekly and end-of-treatment chart checks per AAPM TG-275 recommendations.
source_reference: PRIMARY: AAPM Task Group 275 report (Ford et al., Med Phys 2020;47(6):e236-e272, doi 10.1002/mp.14030), full text at PMC9012523 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9012523/, downloaded and read): practical evidence-based recommendations for physics plan and chart review covering the initial plan and chart check, the weekly chart check, and the end-of-treatment chart check; peer review of prescriptions, target and organ-at-risk contours, dose distributions and on-treatment imaging; second check by a qualified medical physicist; and a request that vendors support automation. SUPPORTING: ASTRO, Safety Is No Accident: A Framework for Quality Radiation Oncology and Care, PDF at https://mdcb.org/sites/mdcb/files/images/SafetyisnoAccident.pdf (official document mirror, downloaded).
expert_raw_materials: TPS plan files (structures, dose distributions, DVH), the prescription, chart documents, on-treatment imaging, machine QA data
usage_permissions: Institutional quality program documents; TG-275 and the ASTRO framework are society-published open guidance documents
task_input: A new draft treatment plan plus the patient chart for the physics review queue
professional_operations: Initial check: verify prescription and authorization, review contours, dose distribution and DVH against constraints, check plan parameters and independent machine data; weekly check: review imaged fractions, shifts, and doses delivered; end-of-treatment check: verify record completeness and write the summary; document every finding and require correction before treatment proceeds
expected_deliverable: A signed physicist review record (initial, weekly, end-of-treatment) with corrections communicated to the treatment team
success_criteria: Plan errors caught before or at the first fraction; zero unreviewed charts; weekly checks documented per policy
verification_approach: Second check by another qualified medical physicist; peer review rounds of prescriptions, contours and dose distributions; chart audits; incident learning reporting such as ASTRO RO-ILS
platform_dependencies: A commercial treatment planning system, a record-and-verify or oncology information system, physics QA devices (ion chamber, EPID), on institutional Windows infrastructure
blocking_risks: Plan files and charts live in commercial TPS and OIS products with proprietary formats and DICOM-RT extensions; full automation needs vendor APIs; a missed error can harm a patient, so qualified human accountability remains a regulatory requirement, which pushes the workflow toward task redesign rather than direct Linux re-hosting
expert_capability: Qualified medical physicist status (board or national registration), TPS operation, dose constraint knowledge
cross_domain_overlap: clinical_informatics covers OIS integrations; med_onco_wf03 (RECIST on follow-up imaging) is complementary. No S1-02A overlap, the A round has zero health rows; this is clinical plan QA, not imaging software engineering.
granularity_check: Right granularity: a bounded recurring per-plan and per-week review task.

workflow_title: RECIST 1.1 tumor response assessment: lesion selection, measurement, and response categorization
occupation_scope: Radiologist measures the lesions; oncologist applies the categories to treatment decisions; trial sites use the same workflow with imaging cores
workflow_summary: A radiologist selects measurable target lesions (maximum 5, maximum 2 per organ), measures their diameters at each timepoint with the same modality, computes the sum of diameters, and assigns CR, PR, SD or PD by RECIST 1.1 thresholds so the oncologist can decide whether the treatment continues.
source_reference: PRIMARY: RECIST Working Group page (https://recist.eortc.org/recist-1-1/, fetched): documents the RECIST 1.1 workflow rules including target lesion selection, measurability (CT 10 mm with slice thickness 5 mm or less), nodal short axis of at least 15 mm as measurable, CR and PR (at least 30 percent decrease) versus PD (at least 20 percent increase plus 5 mm absolute increase) versus SD, rescanning with the same modality at predefined intervals, plus clarification FAQ topics (coalesced lesions, nodal reappearance, PET). GUIDELINE PDF: https://recist.eortc.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/14/2025/12/RECISTGuidelines.pdf (downloaded and read; Eisenhauer et al., revised RECIST guideline version 1.1).
expert_raw_materials: Baseline and follow-up CT or MRI DICOM sets, the lesion list, measurement calipers, prior response summaries
usage_permissions: RECIST criteria are openly published by the RECIST Working Group (EORTC, NCI, CCTG partnership) for free use with citation (recist.eortc.org)
task_input: The baseline scan with the existing lesion selection plus the current follow-up scan
professional_operations: Review baseline and current scans; confirm the target lesion selection (up to 5 lesions, at most 2 per organ); measure the longest diameters including nodal short axis; compute the sum and percent change; apply new-lesion and non-target progression rules; assign CR, PR, SD or PD; perform the confirmatory scan for CR or PR in non-randomized settings; document the response worksheet
expected_deliverable: A response assessment report with per-lesion measurements, the sum, the percent change, and the RECIST category
success_criteria: Correct category by the published thresholds; measurements consistent with the same-modality same-thickness rules; inter-reader agreement met in audited trial contexts
verification_approach: Independent second measurement; trial imaging core-lab adjudication; immunotherapy-adapted reassessment with iRECIST where indicated
platform_dependencies: PACS or DICOM viewer with measurement tooling; trial case report form systems; optional dedicated RECIST tracking software
blocking_risks: Measurement tooling is embedded in proprietary viewers; slice thickness and modality consistency constraints apply; new-lesion judgment remains interpretive, so automation is conditional on DICOM tooling and human adjudication
expert_capability: Cross-sectional imaging measurement discipline, mastery of RECIST 1.1 rules and their FAQ clarifications

workflow_title: Immunotherapy-related toxicity grading, assessment, and management per the ESMO 2022 clinical practice guideline
occupation_scope: Medical oncologist leads assessment and treatment; oncology nurse monitors symptoms; relevant organ specialists consulted per the algorithms
